title: MercadoLibre Plunged After Earnings. Here's Why I'm Not Selling.
detail:
MercadoLibre Plunged After Earnings. Here's Why I'm Not Selling.
Matt Frankel, CFP®, The Motley Fool
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:42 AM MST 5 min read
MELI
^IXIC
Trade MELI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) fell by 12% on Nov. 5, the day after the company's third-quarter earnings came in below analysts' expectations. That leaves the stock more than 40% below its all-time high. Of course, some of it was due to broader market pressure, as the Nasdaq Composite had its worst day in years, but there were also numbers in the company's results that drove the decline. MercadoLibre is one of the largest investments in my own portfolio, so naturally, I'm not thrilled about the drop. But I'm not planning to sell a single share.

Another quarter of rapid growth

MercadoLibre's revenue grew 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, or 41% on a currency-neutral basis, slightly ahead of analysts' estimates. Its commerce business grew revenue 47%, and its fintech business grew 42%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The underlying metrics were strong, too. Gross merchandise volume (GMV), the total value of goods sold on its marketplace, rose 33% on a currency-neutral basis. Total payment volume through Mercado Pago grew 53% to $109 billion, and the fintech platform now has about 93 million monthly active users, up 29% from a year ago.

So why did the stock fall?

In a nutshell, the problem was profitability. MercadoLibre earned $8.83 per share in the third quarter, below the roughly $9.30 analysts expected, and its operating margin shrank to 6.3% from 9.8% a year earlier.

Based on that, you might be wondering whether something is going wrong with the business, but I don't see any massive red flags. MercadoLibre increased its fulfillment capacity by almost 20% from the second quarter, offered free shipping on more orders, and increased marketing spending in Brazil. As CFO Martín de los Santos explained on the call, "The quarter when you are building capacity, you don't have the revenues yet, so you have the cost." He also said he expects margins to recover next quarter.

But the two biggest reasons MercadoLibre's operating margin fell year-over-year were higher operating costs and bad debts from the rapidly growing credit portfolio.

The lending business looks healthy

Speaking of the credit portfolio, it's also worth noting that side of the business held up. MercadoLibre's loan portfolio grew 62% to $17.9 billion, and the rate of loans 15 to 90 days past due was 7%, roughly unchanged from the prior quarter and close to historical lows, according to management. Management also said it's being a bit more conservative with new loans in Brazil and Argentina, which I like to see when a loan book is growing this quickly. There were higher rates of bad debt, but that's a function of the rapid growth of the credit portfolio, not of deteriorating credit quality.

MercadoLibre (MELI) Is Considered a Good Investment by Brokers: Is That True?

The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about MercadoLibre (MELI).

MercadoLibre currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.42, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 20 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.42 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 20 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 15 are Strong Buy and one is Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 75% and 5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for MELI
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for MELI

Check price target & stock forecast for MercadoLibre here>>>

The ABR suggests buying MercadoLibre, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Investing.com -- MercadoLibre Inc (MELI) reported Q3 2026 on Nov 4. Revenue was strong, but EPS missed and margins shrank again. Shares were at $1,514.52 (-12.95%) as of Nov 5, 1:11 PM EST, near the low end of a 52-week range of $1,469.01–$2,342.

MercadoLibre Inc (MELI): $1,514.52 (Market Cap: ~$76.5B) || EPS $8.83 vs $9.34 est (-5.46%) || Revenue $10.75B vs $10.69B est (+45% YoY) || Operating margin 6.3% vs 12.2% a year earlier

Sources: Investing.com earnings report, Nov 4 and Nov 5 move.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Questions Answered

Is growth intact? Yes. GMV rose 38% to $23B and payment volume rose 53% to $109B. The company said it gained share in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina.

Is credit scaling? Yes. The portfolio is near $18B (+62% YoY). Fintech users grew 29% to 93M. Cantor said net interest margin after losses was stable despite record card issuance (Cantor note, Nov 5).

Is the balance sheet fine? It looks fine. The company completed a $1B investment-grade bond issue in September.

Do low-cost shipments pay? Raymond James noted they turned variable contribution positive for the first time (Nov 5).

Questions Still Open

Have margins bottomed? Operating margin fell from 7.0% last quarter to 6.3%. Net income was $448M (4.2% margin). Net shipping margin is down about 200 bps of GMV since Q1 2025.

What is driving the squeeze? Fulfillment square footage grew almost 20% QoQ. Free-shipping thresholds were lowered. Sales and marketing rose to 11.6% of revenue from 11.2% on Brazil's affiliate program.

Is Mexico slowing? FX-neutral GMV rose only 21%, with tax reform and weak consumption cited.

Is the miss a pattern? EPS missed in 3 of the last 4 quarters. The Q1 miss of -12.17% led to an -11.33% reaction.

Are new credit cohorts profitable? Per Raymond James, the 2026 Brazil card cohort is still loss-making and the 2025 cohort is at break-even.

Estimates Are Sliding

Consensus EPS is down 6.75% over 90 days and 33.37% over a year. Revenue estimates are up 15.29% over the same year. Analysts are paying for growth but are cutting their profit expectations.

Next Catalysts

Q4 results: tentatively Feb 25, 2027. Consensus is EPS $11.17 and revenue $11.96B. Peak-season fulfillment utilization will test whether margins stabilize.

Margin trajectory: Raymond James expects the investment cycle to ease as fulfillment utilization and slow-shipping economics improve. Cantor cut its FY2027 EBIT estimate on near-term investments.

Competition: the previous week's preview piece cited Chinese rivals gaining after the removal of the 20% import tax on items under $50. It also said Shopee has launched four-hour delivery in São Paulo (preview, Nov 4).

Credit seasoning: a slower ratio of new cards to aged cohorts would help the credit margin.

Analyst targets: targets were cut but ratings stayed bullish. Examples are Cantor at $2,000, Scotiabank at $2,300 and StoneX at $2,260.

title: MercadoLibre Pays Up to Win Shoppers’ Loyalty
detail:
MercadoLibre Pays Up to Win Shoppers’ Loyalty
The Rule Breakers Team, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 10:03 AM MST 4 min read
MELI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

After the market closed yesterday, MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) reported third-quarter revenue of $10.75 billion, up 45% from a year ago. Operating income fell 6% to $676 million, and the operating margin shrank to 6.3% from 9.8% a year earlier. The stock fell about 6% in pre-market trading this morning.

Much of that lost profit went to shoppers. For Team Rule Breakers, which has recommended the stock twice in Stock Advisor since 2023, that choice is a direct test of what draws customers to a business and keeps them there.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The fifth of six Rule Breakers Traits is: Strong Consumer Appeal

Shoppers today face more choices than they can sort through. Brands that let people pick one trusted place to shop and pay can earn deep loyalty, and the best ones build raving fans. That loyalty rarely shows up in financial statements, which is one reason the market can overlook it.

Where the Profit Went

Last year, MercadoLibre lowered the order size needed for free shipping in Brazil. Shoppers responded by buying cheaper items more often. Items sold in Brazil rose 45% in the quarter, but each package now brings in less revenue. The company also grew its warehouse space by almost 20% in a single quarter ahead of the holiday season and spent more on affiliate marketing in Brazil. Management said it gained market share in Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina.

Its fintech business grew quickly, too. Monthly active users rose 29% to 93 million, and the credit portfolio grew 62% to nearly $18 billion. The company sets aside money for expected loan losses as soon as it extends a loan. Interest income arrives later, so fast credit growth tends to weigh on profit today.

When Perks Become Expectations

Once shoppers get used to free shipping, they may resist paying for it again. MercadoLibre could then struggle to restore its margins without losing some of the customers it just won. Rivals such as Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) also compete hard in Brazil, which makes pulling back on perks riskier.

The other markets and the lending business carry their own risks. In Mexico, tax changes and weaker spending slowed growth. Late loans held steady in the quarter, but a credit book growing this fast could cause trouble if Latin American borrowers come under strain.

Is the Appeal Worth the Price?

Coupang (CPNG) stock rose 12.0% on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 1.6%. The advance came the day after the e-commerce company reported third-quarter results on November 3, during a session where all five companies on its Trefis peer list also climbed. So what did Coupang's quarter show?

Coupang Beat Sales Estimates With Mixed Per-Share Results

Coupang's revenue reached $9.96 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, clearing the analysts' consensus estimate of $9.76 billion. Sales grew 7.5% from a year earlier. Measured at constant exchange rates, management put growth at 11%, exceeding the 8% to 9% range it had guided to.

Against estimates, the per-share results proved mixed. Coupang recorded $248 million in costs during the quarter from a July fire at one of its fulfillment centers. Including the fire, the company posted a loss of $0.28 per share. Excluding it, the loss was about $0.18 per share. That missed the $0.09 loss in our earnings calendar's consensus but beat the Zacks consensus of a $0.23 loss.

Management also discussed Product Commerce, its main retail business. The segment generated an adjusted EBITDA margin of 4.6%, down about 420 basis points from a year earlier. Management tied part of the decline to last year's data incident, after which some WOW members left. Management believes the third quarter was the low point for that margin and expects it to return to about pre-incident levels by the middle of 2027.

Did Coupang Rise Alone Or With Other Retailers?

Coupang climbed with other retailers, advancing further than any of its five Trefis peers. Etsy gained 7.1% and Amazon added 6.1% that session, and XLY, the SPDR fund for consumer discretionary stocks, rose 4.3%.

Where Does Coupang Stock Stand Now?

Such a large advance is rare for Coupang. Only one other session in the previous 365 days brought a gain at least this big: a 14.1% rise on June 11, 2026.

The stock remains far below where it traded a year ago. Coupang stock lost 46.9% over the twelve months to November 4, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 14.9%. Its highest close during that period was $32.13 on November 4, 2025, and its lowest was $13.75 on September 28, 2026. The stock has climbed back part of the way over the past month, returning 18.2% from October 6 to November 4 while the S&P 500 lost 1.6%.

Coupang's next report will cover the fourth quarter of 2026. Management expects revenue growth of 13% to 14% at constant exchange rates for that quarter, and that growth rate is the number to watch.

That habit is being built on Brazil's low-priced orders, the ones Sea Limited (SE:NYSE) chases with Shopee. And the quarter's steady credit sets a bar for Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE).

Where the profit went

Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, ahead of estimates. But EPS missed as operating income fell 6% to $676 million on more free shipping, almost 20% more fulfillment space ahead of the holidays, and extra affiliate marketing in Brazil.

Paying for the habit

MercadoLibre cut Brazil's free shipping threshold to R$19 from R$79 in June 2025, and items sold there have grown more than 40% for five straight quarters since.

But cheaper items earn less each, so net shipping margin has lost about 200 basis points of gross merchandise volume since early 2025.

The margin was sliding well before the third quarter, when it fell to 6.3% from 9.8%:

The bill is starting to shrink

Brazil's cost per shipment fell 5% from a year earlier in local currency. And in September, free, slow shipments priced from R$19 to R$79 covered their variable costs as a group for the first time.

That push lands on Shopee, whose Brazil capacity Sea grew 60% in a year. If Shopee's Brazil growth slows next week, MercadoLibre's shipping spend is buying share.

Credit held up, too: MercadoLibre's 15-90 day NPL stayed around 7.0%. Nu's improved to 4.8% in the second quarter, and its report next week will show whether its Brazil book is as steady.
